messages:
emma: FYI Verdant reported repeated 429s and high tail latency during their marketing blast this morning (09:05-09:22 UTC). They say their reserved slab is 8 nodes, baseline ~85 QPS, observed peak ~420 QPS. Customer says retries ballooned costs. Posting snippets they shared below.

ashwin: Confirming I can see the alerts for 429 spikes in our monitoring. Summary from metrics: aggregated QPS matched their numbers, autoscaler did not scale above 8 until ~09:12, then scaled to 10 by 09:18. Per-GPU util on two pods hit ~96% for ~3m. Looks like headroom exhausted and queueing caused 429s.

luis: Requesting their autoscale policy and model variant. Could be that their target_util is too high for request bursts (continuous batching keeps latency down but single-request bursts push token latency).

emma: They provided autoscale config: 
```yaml
min_replicas: 6
max_replicas: 16
target_gpu_utilization: 0.75
scale_cooldown_sec: 120
scale_window: 60s
burst_capacity: disabled
```
They also included a sample failing request (headers redacted): 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
 -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","prompt":"...", "max_tokens":512}'
```
Customer says 429 body: `\{"error\":\"capacity_exceeded\",\"message\":\"reserved_slab_throttling\"\}`

olivia: Two immediate observations: 1) target_gpu_utilization 0.75 + min_replicas 6 with baseline 85 QPS probably okay, but their burst ratio (peak/baseline ~5x) needs warmup/burst capacity. 2) burst_capacity flagged disabled — that prevents short spikes from getting temporary headroom.

ashwin: Repro steps I ran in staging (using local replay of Verdant traffic): ramped from 80 QPS -> 420 QPS over 60s. Autoscaler behavior: didn't add replicas before requests started queuing because the control loop uses a 60s window and 120s cooldown. By the time new pods are ready (POD startup ~45-70s), their queue produced 429s.

luis: Logs from the runtime show many requests hitting the per-pod in-flight queue limit and our per-tenant concurrency limiter kicked in with 429. Example from runtime logs: 
```
[09:10:37] tenant=verdant shard=reserved-slab-8 request_id=... in_flight=64 max_in_flight=64 -> throttle(429)
[09:10:40] pod=verdant-3 gpu_util=95.8% latency_p95=1.2s tokens/sec=60
```

emma: Customer also flagged unexpected billing jump. They retried 3x on client side when they saw 429s. Their bill shows token/unit usage spike between 09:05-09:25. They want root cause + credits.

olivia: Short-term mitigations to propose -> 1) enable burst_capacity on their slab to allow soft burst to max_replicas for X minutes, 2) temporarily bump min_replicas to 10 for next 48 hours, 3) reduce target_gpu_utilization to 0.6 so autoscaler is more aggressive, 4) ask them to implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter to reduce retry storms.

ashwin: I can push a one-off change to enable burst_capacity and set min_replicas=10 right now if billing team approves emergency configuration change for Verdant. Need @ops-bot to create an approval ticket.

ops-bot: Approval ticket created: TICKET-62891. Marking as P1 config-change request for customer Verdant. Please include expected timeframe and rollback plan.

luis: For longer-term: recommend schedule-based warmup before big campaigns: allow pre-scale window with synthetic warmup traffic (low-cost warmup tokens using cheap model variant), and add a scale_policy: "prewarm_on_schedule" in Console. Also consider enabling KV cache warm start if they use chat with long prefixes.

emma: Customer asked for reproduction steps so they can validate after changes. Suggested minimal repro we ran: 
1) Set a client to replay their 10-minute campaign traffic at real timestamps to a test slab. 
2) Ramp baseline 80 QPS -> 420 QPS in 60s. 
3) Observe throttle events and pod spin-up time. 

ashwin: I added exact command I used to simulate burst (wrk): 
```bash
wrk -t8 -c200 -d70s -s scripts/verdant_ramp.lua --latency http://staging-inference.local/generate
```
Lua script ramps from 80 to 420 QPS over 60s and posts sample payload.

luis: Also attached SQL to pull our metrics for the tenant if you need to validate: 
```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute, sum(qps) as qps, max(gpu_util) as max_gpu
FROM inference_metrics
WHERE tenant = 'verdant' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-09-15 09:00' AND '2025-09-15 09:30'
GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute;
```

olivia: Proposed resolution plan (short bullets for EM/pager): 
- Immediate (hours): enable burst_capacity, bump min_replicas to 10, issue customer credit for retry cost (support->billing).
- Near-term (days): change target_gpu_utilization -> 0.6, reduce scale_cooldown to 60s, enable prewarm schedule for recurring campaigns.
- Long-term (weeks): implement predictive scaling for scheduled campaigns (Console UI + prewarm API), educ customer on client-side retry/backoff and cheaper warmup model.

emma: Customer accepted temporary changes if we can commit to diagnostics + credit. Assigning: ashwin to apply config change, luis to validate metrics and confirm no noisy-neighbor pinhole, olivia to coordinate credit and account comms.

ashwin: Applying change now: enabling burst_capacity=true, min_replicas=10. Will monitor.

ops-bot: Config change applied to tenant=verdant by ashwin at 2025-09-15T09:28:11Z (change_id=chg-94218).

luis: Early signs: no further 429s observed in the next 6 minutes of traffic replay, per-pod gpu_util back to 70-80%. Will continue monitoring for 30m.

emma: Billing note -> support to open billing case and recommend 30% credit for retry-induced tokens pending review. Olivia please post the credit proposal in billing thread.

olivia: Will open billing case and post proposal. Also added action item to update docs: "How to size reserved slabs for high-burst campaigns" with sample policies.

ashwin: Follow-up: we should add an automated check to warn customers when peak/baseline > 3x and burst_capacity is disabled. Filing infra-idea ticket.

emma: Thanks team. Closing loop with Verdant and will share remediation + postmortem once we have billing outcome. :thumbsup:
